biography.plain_text: Roger Samuelsson is a Swedish entrepreneur who built his fortune in medical-device manufacturing. After trading goods from Taiwan, he co-founded SHL Medical in 1989 and turned an early injector contract into a global autoinjector business. He later stepped back from day-to-day management but remains the company's founder and majority owner.

long_biography.plain_text:
Roger Samuelsson grew up in Sweden, studied engineering in Linköping and first visited Taiwan after noticing where his boxing gloves were made. He began exporting local goods to Sweden, moved to Taiwan and co-founded Scandinavian Health Limited in 1989. An injector contract with Upjohn became the company's breakthrough; Samuelsson later bought out his partner and focused the business on autoinjectors.

SHL Medical combined device design with automated manufacturing, helping medicines move from clinics into patients' homes. Samuelsson remained chief executive until 2018, when Ulrich Fässler took over, and he continues as majority shareholder rather than day-to-day operator. The company is now based in Switzerland and supplies leading pharmaceutical groups. Its expansion from a Taiwan trading venture to a global drug-delivery manufacturer is the principal source of Samuelsson's wealth.
